gates: Retain the weighted compiler, restriction, online cache, information-bound and archive-integrity gates. Add exact counterfactual parity against independent per-candidate fixed-baseline simulation for remaining MAP budgets 0,1,2,4. Fixed synthetic costs: acceptance 74 <= 82, rejection 215 > 119, and equality 2 == 2. Verify repeated cost-cache hits add no work. Prefix sharing must preserve every candidate cost; measured selector calls are reported. Runtime repeats the gates and retains their complete proof artifacts, with all compiler/counterfactual memo states and split evaluations in the aggregate limits. No cohort pilot outcomes are computed before freeze.
ledger: One append-only JSONL ledger with sequence, previous-record SHA256, UTC, monotonic time, kind and data; canonical sorted compact JSON hash. Every append flushes and fsyncs before return. Query record is committed before oracle is called; next answer references query hash. Source draws and final results also retained. Never regenerate records after answers. Publish exact raw bytes or deterministic gzip with decompressed hash.

ledger_gate.required: Before new source draws, reproduce fixed8 archived query/answer logical fields in old separate-file and new ledger format. Oracle callbacks must read and verify committed query before returning label; enforce sequence/hash/time/reference replay. Reject altered answer, swapped order, broken chain, and rehashed wrong query-reference fixtures. Charge all serialization/gate costs.

budget.enforcement: Aggregate memo states include tree-compiler states plus counterfactual baseline memo entries; aggregate split evaluations include tree canonical alternatives plus counterfactual MAP partitions. Runtime scientific fixtures contribute the same components. CPU/wall limits include all computations, independent fixture checks, preparation, serialization and monitoring. Any cap, error, missing proof or correctness violation makes the whole study incomplete, retaining every planned case and paid call. No budget extension or reduced-scope claim.

descriptive: Report MAP/tree call components, all guard accept/reject/tie counts, handoff timing, cache/node counts, CPU/wall costs and overlap charges. The original 10,355-call H3br policy remains the primary comparator. H3bs used 10,937 calls on the same examined cases; any comparison with it is descriptive. No case filtering, new draws, independent confirmation or changed accuracy endpoint.
counterfactual: The baseline evaluator receives current candidates, sorted queried-board indices, remaining MAP budget, and immutable candidate predictions/scores. It recursively follows both predicted label branches of each fixed-baseline MAP query, then obtains terminal posterior-tree leaf depths. Every remaining candidate gets its exact remaining-call count. No actual true identity, case ID or archived future answer enters evaluation. Full input identities, branch selections, child result hashes, terminal tree references and per-candidate counts are persisted. Every root is hash-bound in a separate cost-guard ledger event before the real routing decision. Model prediction computations are not actual oracle invocations; all actual MAP/tree labels are still independently paid.
cost_guard: Let weights be the positive integer weights in the current tree proof. Compare int(tree.optimal_cost) with sum(weights[c] * baseline_remaining_calls[c]) using exact integers. A feasible ancestor implies every counterfactual fixed-baseline terminal subset is depth-four separable; a noninformative query or infeasible terminal tree is therefore a correctness failure, not an excluded branch. Cost proof cache keys bind candidates, remaining MAP budget, sorted queried indices, depth, predictions hash, scores hash, selector hash and tree-compiler hash. All branches are retained.
expected_cost_property: The guard implies nonincrease under the prescribed posterior when it accepts. On rejection, the same next MAP query followed by this guarded rule also has no larger expected cost than its fixed-baseline continuation, by backward induction. This conditional optimization property and per-case identification equality are correctness properties. They do not imply a realized 2% finite-cohort reduction, a population effect size or calibration outside the declared model. See GUARD_LEMMA.md.
